description.narrative: he escalation of the Cambodia–Thailand border dispute on 09 December 2025 has triggered widespread civilian displacement across multiple border provinces, creating urgent humanitarian needs and significant protection risks for affected populations. Ongoing airstrikes, shelling, and ground fighting have damaged civilian infrastructure, forced the relocation of displacement sites, and overwhelmed existing safety camps. As a result, tens of thousands of families—predominantly women, children, elderly people, people with disabilities, and female-headed households—are facing acute shortages of safe water, sanitation, shelter, food, and essential non-food items. Outcome 1: Conflict-affected and displaced populations have improved access to life-saving WASH services and live in safer, more dignified conditions. Displaced families—particularly women, children, elderly people, people with disabilities, and female-headed households—have reliable access to safe drinking water, adequate sanitation, and hygiene facilities that reduce public health risks and uphold dignity in overcrowded, most needed, and high-risk camps. Key outcome results include: • Reduced exposure to waterborneand sanitation-related diseases in DIP camps • Improved safety, privacy, and dignity for women and girls through gender-responsive WASH facilities • Increased availability of safe drinking water in camps affected by infrastructure damage and population influx Outcome 2: Displaced households meet immediate basic needs through access to essential shelter materials and non-food items. Conflict-affected families are better protected from environmental exposure and insecurity through access to temporary shelter materials and essential household items, supporting minimum living standards during displacement. Key outcome results include: • Improved shelter conditions in overcrowded or newly relocated camps • Reduced reliance on negative coping mechanisms linked to lack of basic householditems • Enhanced protection and well-being of vulnerable households during displacement

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project#s implementation.
